parsed_profile.title: 7F AND 9F AFT END COMPRESSOR RUBS
parsed_profile.reason_for_revision: To update the technical content of the TIL, including frequency of tip loss and recommendations when discovered.
parsed_profile.purpose: To inform users to monitor equipment operation and condition, and to identify the onset, occurrence, and effects of aft end compressor rubs (when the tip of the rotor blade rubs the casing). Rubs are evident when blade tip material is adversely affected. Information in this TIL is supplemental to information in the Inspection and Maintenance Manual provided with the gas turbine.
parsed_profile.compliance_category_text: Maintenance - Identifies maintenance guidelines or best practices for reliable equipment operation.
scope_of_work: Monitor equipment operation and condition for aft end compressor rubs
Integrate inspection for aft end compressor rubs with yearly scheduled borescope inspection per GER 3620
Observe rotor blade stages 13 through 17 and look for mushroomed material, bluing at the blade tip, and/or markings in the casing area
If rubs or tip loss occur, blending to increase clearances can be performed at Major Inspections (MI) or when the Compressor Discharge Casing (CDC) is removed
During repairs, clearances of rotor blades can be increased radially by tip grinding and polishing, and tip corners repaired by blade blending (typically 20 mils radially)
Following tip grinding/polishing, a penetrant inspection must be performed to ensure no tip cracks are present
service_recommendation_line_items: Follow operating practices per GER 3620 to reduce the potential for rubs on aft end compressor blades
Keep enclosure doors closed during startup, shutdown and normal operation

Be aware that restarting the gas turbine between 2 and 8 hours following a shutdown or trip will cause clearances in the aft end to decrease; include this area in yearly borescope inspections if unit operates this way
Eliminate any potential pipe leaks that may cause quenching of the gas turbine compressor discharge casing
Ensure vent fans and exhaust fans to the gas turbine enclosure are functioning properly such that no local forced convection is taking place at or near the compressor discharge casing
Integrate the inspection for aft end compressor rubs with yearly scheduled borescope inspection per GER 3620; observe rotor blade stages 13 through 17
If rubs or tip loss occur, perform blending at Major Inspection or when CDC is removed; typically remove 20 mils radially to increase clearance and remove heat affected and rolled over material
Following tip grinding/polishing operation, perform penetrant inspection to ensure no tip cracks are present
parsed_profile.completion_criteria_text: Penetrant inspection must confirm no tip cracks are present following tip grinding and polishing operations.
parsed_profile.maintenance_trigger_text: Next Scheduled Outage (Timing Code 6); yearly borescope inspection; Major Inspection or CDC removal for blending repairs.
recommended_interval_or_trigger: Major Inspection (MI) or when Compressor Discharge Casing (CDC) is removed for blending repairs
parsed_profile.usage_counter_requirements_text: Restarting the gas turbine between 2 and 8 hours following a shutdown or trip causes aft end clearances to decrease and may cause tip rubs. Units operating with frequent restarts in this window should include aft end in yearly borescope inspections.
parsed_profile.frame_or_model_applicability_text: All 7F and 9F Heavy Duty Gas Turbines
parsed_profile.hardware_or_part_configuration_text: Compressor rotor blades in rows 13, 14, and 15 are primarily affected. Stages 13 through 17 should be observed during inspection.
parsed_profile.prerequisite_outage_or_inspection_contex: Yearly borescope inspection per GER 3620; Major Inspection or CDC removal required for blending repairs.

reference_documents.context: Operating practices and yearly borescope inspection guidelines to reduce potential for aft end compressor rubs

severity_signals: Very low risk to unit operation and reliability
No performance impact and no forced outages experienced
Heat generated from a rub can lower the local material fatigue strength of the blade resulting in material tip loss in the event of another rub
failure_consequences: Blade tip material loss (typically less than 1/16 inch² in area)
Bluing at blade tip indicating heat affected zone
Lowered local material fatigue strength potentially leading to further tip loss on subsequent rubs
parsed_profile.risk_summary: Aft end compressor rubs and/or tip loss pose very low risk to unit operation and reliability. No performance impact and no forced outages have been experienced. Rubs are primarily induced by frequent restarts between 2 to 8 hours after shutdown due to thermal compression of the casing relative to the rotor decreasing clearances.

source_snippets.snippet: To inform users to monitor equipment operation and condition, and to identify the onset, occurrence, and effects of aft end compressor rubs (when the tip of the rotor blade rubs the casing).
Aft end rubs and/or tip loss pose very low risk to unit operation and reliability. No performance impact and no forced outages have been experienced due to this issue.
If rubs or tip loss do occur, blending to increase clearances can be performed at Major Inspections (MI) or when the Compressor Discharge Casing (CDC) is removed.
restarting the gas turbine between two (2) and eight (8) hours following a shutdown or trip will cause the clearances in the aft end to decrease.
Following this operation, a penetrant inspection must be performed to ensure no tip cracks are present.
Rotor blades in rows 13, 14, and 15 are primarily affected.
